pages.text: There is $(bold)no random ore$(). Geolosys places metal in deposits: each of one kind, each large, each at its own depth. Iron may be a ten-minute walk; zinc may be the next valley over.$(br2)This is deliberate. Ore that is somewhere else is why wagons, ships and eventually trains exist.

Look for $(bold)samples$(): small rock clusters lying on the surface that show what is below. Dig straight down from a sample and you reach the deposit.$(br2)Ore blocks drop $(bold)clusters$(), not raw ore. Smelt them, or crush and wash them in Create for more.
One cluster, one ingot in a furnace. Create's crushing wheels and washing give more per cluster once you have them.

$(bold)Where metal lives$() near the surface:$(li)$(bold)Everywhere:$() iron (hematite), copper (malachite), coal, aluminum (bauxite)$(li)$(bold)Mountains:$() zinc, platinum, beryl$(li)$(bold)Dry country:$() gold, lapis; $(bold)sandy:$() tin (cassiterite)$(li)$(bold)Plains:$() lead and silver (galena); $(bold)marsh:$() nickel (limonite)

$(bold)Deep down it evens out.$() Below about Y -16, in the deepslate, lead and silver, nickel, platinum, tin and gold lie in their own deposits under $(italic)every$() biome: smaller than the regional ones, but a cave that runs deep enough finds them in its walls.$(br2)Deepslate ore also gives one to two clusters a block, not one. The regional deposits are the rich ones; the deep is the road for everyone else.
